clue.text: What poor comedians do that's ridiculous

definitions.meaning: a weak comic fails to raise any laughter from the audience
a scornful exclamation dismissing a claim as absurd

explanation.surface: A reviewer's sneer at feeble stand-up acts, calling their efforts absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal description of failing comics and the common scoffing retort to nonsense.

clue.text: Announcer about to retire after failing medical

indicators.note: the reversed piece follows the rearranged one
the word medical falls apart, signalling a rearrangement
retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A broadcaster forced to step down after failing a health check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges medical into DECLAIM; 'to retire' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks out rhetorically or makes pronouncements, as an announcer does.

clue.text: Born to stop Oliver ultimately wanting more?

parts.note: née marks a birth name
to die is to stop, as an engine does

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: A birth halts Oliver in the end, who keeps wanting more.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark nods to Oliver Twist asking for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more in need means wanting more, a comparative adjective.

clue.text: Diverse staff in firm initially getting on

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: getting on means ageing, old

explanation.surface: A varied workforce at a company that is getting older.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means many and various, a synonym of diverse.

clue.text: One's told to seal a letter to Zorba

indicators.note: told signals that the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: with One's before it, one who is to seal a bottle or pen by putting its top on: a capper

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to seal a letter addressed to Zorba.
explanation.walkthrough: Zorba the Greek, the novel's hero, stands for any Greek; the 'letter' is an alphabet character.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth character in the alphabet a Greek like Zorba uses.

clue.text: Metal tops for each stopper I placed in large bottle

indicators.note: the letters are put inside the bottle word

parts.note: a magnum is a double-size wine bottle

indicators.note: the tops of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Metal caps for each cork are placed in a big bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a light silvery chemical element, a metal used in alloys and flares.

clue.text: Spare fire

definitions.meaning: to spare is to excuse from punishment
to fire a gun or set off a firework

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to excuse someone and to discharge a gun or detonate something.

clue.text: Visionary Scot supporting prize university put up

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below
in a down clue, putting up reverses the letters

parts.note: a pot is a prize cup
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scottish dreamer backs a university put up for an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns POTU into UTOP; IAN is underneath it in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic and visionary, imagining a perfect society.

clue.text: Refined individual in Holland cleared out

indicators.note: the word for an individual goes inside
with its contents cleared out, only the outer letters remain

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A single person in the Netherlands has been emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpened or perfected, as a skill polished by practice.

clue.text: Be inclined to enter contest free from corruption

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, so the leaning word sits within the trophy word

parts.note: a cup is a sporting contest, as in the FA Cup
to lean is to be inclined

explanation.surface: Advice to tilt towards entering a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up a town or sport is to rid it of crime and corruption, a common idiom.

clue.text: Fledglings do it to descend from mount

definitions.meaning: young birds grow their first soft fluffy feathers
to dismount, climbing off a horse

explanation.surface: Young birds are taught to climb off a perch or mount.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is down as in fine feathers: fledglings acquire it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismounting means stepping off to the ground; the first reading takes down as the fluffy plumage of chicks.

clue.text: The greatest length spanned by trunk road

indicators.note: something spanned by another is bridged across, so it sits within it

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest trunk road, London to Edinburgh, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A boast about the longest stretch of a major highway.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; the digit 1 is taken as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, the boxer, famously called himself 'The Greatest'.

clue.text: Mood in which artist visualises his painting exhibited?

definitions.text: in which artist visualises his painting exhibited?
definitions.meaning: a painter imagines the border that will surround the canvas on the gallery wall

explanation.surface: A painter dreams of how the finished canvas will look on display.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means one's mental state or outlook; read literally it is a picture border imagined in the head.

clue.text: Better technology gains popularity, apparently

parts.note: more people approve of it, as if counting likes on social media
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Tech is finally winning people over and that is an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the last two pieces say that more folk like the tech.
explanation.definitionFit: An approving exclamation meaning 'that is an improvement', closer to what was wanted.

clue.text: Make no response as English in fort surrender

parts.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the surrender word

parts.note: to quit is to give up

explanation.surface: An Englishman in a besieged fort gives no reply to a call to surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay silent is to give no response.

clue.text: Spur-of-the-moment children's game

definitions.meaning: sudden, done without planning, as in a quick decision
a card game where players call out on seeing matching cards

explanation.definitionFit: A hasty decision is called this; it is also a card game for children where identical cards are matched.

clue.text: Chivalry the undoing of poet's isle?

indicators.note: undoing the words' letters breaks them up for rearrangement

explanation.surface: A poet's island reached its ruin through excessive courtesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal courtesy and good manners, close to old-fashioned chivalry.

clue.text: Injured pussycat not caught, tip of tail remains

indicators.note: injured means hurt or damaged, signalling a rearrangement
not means the letter is left out

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the tip is the first letter

explanation.surface: A hurt cat escapes capture and its tail stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not caught' takes C from pussycat; 'Injured' rearranges PUSSYAT into STAYSPU.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put means to remain where one is.

clue.text: Fortieth game to one side

parts.note: RU is rugby union
by means aside, as in 'put by' or 'stand by'

explanation.surface: A game played on the fortieth occasion off to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: The gem traditionally marks a fortieth wedding anniversary.

clue.text: Danced and jeered, serviceman having come in

indicators.note: one piece has entered the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: booed means jeered
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A crowd danced and jeered as a soldier arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To boogie is to dance to pop music, so this is its past tense.

clue.text: Where limitless change of climate is keeping air out

indicators.note: without its limits, the first and last letters of the word are dropped
a change of the letters calls for rearranging them

explanation.surface: A place where unchecked climate change is keeping the air away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitless' trims Where to HER; 'change of' rearranges climate into METICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An airtight seal is so called, after the alchemist Hermes Trismegistus.

clue.text: Mobile weapon cups turned up during search

indicators.note: during places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up reverses the letters

parts.note: a bra has cups

explanation.surface: Cups turn up in a search that uncovers a hidden weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes ARB from BRA, placed in COMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle packed with explosives is a weapon that moves.

clue.text: Politician leading one party shows capacity for it

indicators.note: the politician comes first in the order

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal politician
I is the Roman numeral one
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A politician leading a party displays some capacity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the coy word for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire, so the capacity for sex, 'it' being the euphemism.

clue.text: Imminence of crime one's relinquished after rest

indicators.note: the crime piece follows the rest piece

parts.note: a prop is a support something rests on

indicators.note: something relinquished is given up, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: iniquity means wickedness or a sin
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: How close a crime is, once someone has given it up after a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relinquished' removes one I from INIQUITY, leaving INQUITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nearness, in time or place, so closeness of an approaching event.

clue.text: Primate's instruction to reader devouring scriptures

definitions.note: the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: one piece swallows the other

parts.note: PTO means please turn over
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A bishop's note to a reader buried in Bible study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop; it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A potto is a slow-moving West African primate related to lorises.

clue.text: First person to denounce religion

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun
to slam is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: The first man to condemn a faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A major world faith, founded by Muhammad.

clue.text: Track turning back to some extent

indicators.note: read back means read from right to left
only part of the word is used, its opening letters

explanation.surface: A path that winds round on itself a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' picks TUR from turning; 'back' makes it read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove worn by wheels is a track, as in a cart road.

clue.text: Can it be stopped by Liberal returning capital?

indicators.note: going back, so the whole construction is read in reverse
a phrase stopped by a word has it plugged inside

parts.note: a question meaning 'is it?'

explanation.surface: A doubtful question about whether a Liberal comeback could halt something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' applies to the whole stopped question, not just to Liberal, which is where solvers first look.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Georgia in the Caucasus.

clue.text: China revolutionised the best IT kit

indicators.note: turned round in a revolution, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate, i.e. pal
the tops means the very best

explanation.surface: A boast that China has transformed the finest computing equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' means mate in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate); 'revolutionised' turns PAL round.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable computers are information technology equipment, so items of IT kit.

clue.text: Soldier of the Great War, ex-Tory MP in rendition of Let It Be

parts.note: Con is a Conservative; old means former

indicators.note: a rendition is a performance or version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former Conservative MP sings the Beatles' 'Let It Be' about a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendition of' rearranges MP and LETITBE into TEMPTIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the British Expeditionary Force of 1914 took the name from the Kaiser's alleged jibe.
